title: Encapsulated `Student` Class with Validation
problemStatement: Design a `Student` class with `name` (non-empty), `rollNo` (positive integer), and `cgpa` (`0.0` to `10.0`). Reject invalid updates cleanly without corrupting state, and provide `printProfile() const`.
hint: Validate inside both the constructor and `setCgpa()`.
explanation: Constructor enforces core invariants (`rollNo_ > 0`, non-empty `name_`), while `setCgpa` guards range `[0.0, 10.0]`. Getters are marked `const` so `const Student&` works.
dryRun: `s` initializes with `(101, "Aarav", 8.75)`. `setCgpa(12.0)` returns `false`, leaving `cgpa_` at `8.75`. `printProfile()` prints `8.75`.
complexity: Time $O(1)$ per operation (plus $O(N)$ string move/copy); Space $O(N)$ for name.
commonMistakes: Leaving `cgpa_` uninitialized if `setCgpa` rejects, or forgetting `const` on getters.
followUp: *Why throw in the constructor instead of returning `bool`?* (Constructors have no return value; throwing prevents half-valid objects from existing.)

title: `Rectangle` Class with Delegating Constructors
problemStatement: Create a `Rectangle` class supporting default (`1x1`), square (`side x side`), and general (`w x h`) construction without duplicating validation logic, plus `area()` and `perimeter()`.
constraints: Use modern C++17, avoid memory leaks, preserve const-correctness.
hint: Delegate `Rectangle()` and `Rectangle(double side)` to `Rectangle(double w, double h)`.
explanation: C++11 delegating constructors route all initialization through a single canonical 2-arg constructor, ensuring the `>= 1.0` guard lives in only one place.
commonMistakes: Trying to initialize `width_` *and* delegate in the same initializer list (illegal in C++).
followUp: *Should `Rectangle(double side)` be marked `explicit`?* (Usually yes, unless implicit `double -> Rectangle` conversion is desired.)

title: Fluent `QueryBuilder` Using `this` Pointer
problemStatement: Implement a `QueryBuilder` supporting chained calls like `q.select("name").from("users").where("age > 18").build();`.
constraints: Use modern C++17, avoid memory leaks, preserve const-correctness.
hint: Return `QueryBuilder&` and `return *this;` from each builder step.
explanation: Returning `QueryBuilder&` ensures `.from(...)` and `.where(...)` mutate the exact same `q` object instead of temporary copies.
dryRun: `select` sets `cols_="name"` -> `from` sets `table_="users"` -> `where` sets `cond_="age > 18"` -> `build()` concatenates string.
commonMistakes: Returning `QueryBuilder` by value (breaks chaining on original object).
followUp: *How does `build()` work if `from()` was forgotten?* (Production builders validate `table_` is non-empty and throw `std::logic_error`.)
expectedStdout: SELECT name FROM users WHERE age > 18

title: Object Counter with `inline static` Member & `static` Function
problemStatement: Create a `Session` class that tracks how many `Session` objects are currently **alive** in memory (including copies!) and total ever created.
constraints: Use modern C++17, avoid memory leaks, preserve const-correctness.
hint: Increment `alive` in *both* default and copy constructors, and decrement in `~Session()`.
explanation: Forgetting the copy/move constructors is a classic bug—if `s2 = s1` ran the compiler's copy constructor, `~s2` would decrement `alive_` even though `s2` never incremented it!
dryRun: `s1`: alive=1, total=1. `s2`: alive=2, total=2. `s3`: alive=3, total=3. Block exits: `s3, s2` die -> alive=1. Wait: in `main` above, output is `Alive: 1 | Total: 3`! (Inside the block it was `Alive: 3`, after block `Alive: 1`.)
commonMistakes: Only incrementing in `Session()` and forgetting `Session(const Session&)`, making `alive_` go negative!
followUp: *How would you make this counter thread-safe?* (Use `inline static std::atomic<int> alive_{0};`.)

title: `Time` Class with Normalization and `const` Correctness
problemStatement: Create a `Time(h, m, s)` class that normalizes overflow seconds/minutes (e.g., `Time(1, 70, 90)` -> `02:11:30`) and provides `addSeconds(int s)`.
constraints: Use modern C++17, avoid memory leaks, preserve const-correctness.
hint: Write one `private` `normalize()` helper called by both constructor and `addSeconds()`.
explanation: Converting to total seconds modulo `86400` handles multi-minute or negative wraparound cleanly in one place.
commonMistakes: Using `%` directly on negative numbers without `((total % 86400) + 86400) % 86400`.
followUp: *How would you overload `operator+` to add two `Time` durations?*

title: Explicit `Distance` Converter Class
problemStatement: Create a `Meters` class with an `explicit` constructor so raw `double` values cannot silently convert into `Meters`, plus `toKilometers() const` and `toCentimeters() const`.
constraints: Use modern C++17, avoid memory leaks, preserve const-correctness.
hint: Mark `explicit Meters(double m)`.
explanation: `explicit` prevents accidental unit bugs like `printDist(5)` where `5` could be miles or meters.
dryRun: `Meters(2500)` stores `2500.0`; `toKilometers()` returns `2.5`; `toCentimeters()` returns `250000`.
commonMistakes: Omitting `explicit` on single-argument constructors.
followUp: *What happens if you mark a conversion operator like `explicit operator double() const`?* (Blocks `double d = m;` while allowing `static_cast<double>(m)`.)

title: Custom Copy Constructor Tracking Calls on `Point`
problemStatement: Implement a `Point(x, y)` class with a custom copy constructor and compute Euclidean distance to another `Point` passed by `const&` (without triggering unnecessary copies).
constraints: Use modern C++17, avoid memory leaks, preserve const-correctness.
hint: Use `std::hypot(dx, dy)` from `<cmath>`.
explanation: `distanceTo(const Point&)` avoids invoking the copy constructor, and `std::hypot` prevents intermediate squaring overflow.
commonMistakes: Passing `other` by value in `distanceTo(Point other)` or omitting `const`.
followUp: *Why is `std::hypot(dx, dy)` safer than `std::sqrt(dx*dx + dy*dy)`?* (Avoids overflow on huge doubles.)

title: RAII Scope Timer Using Constructor & Destructor
problemStatement: Build a `ScopeTimer` class that starts a clock in its constructor and automatically prints elapsed microseconds when it goes out of scope.
constraints: Use modern C++17, avoid memory leaks, preserve const-correctness.
hint: Store `std::chrono::steady_clock::time_point` in the constructor, compute delta in `~ScopeTimer()`.
explanation: Even if a function returns early or throws an exception, `~ScopeTimer()` guarantees the timing log executes.
dryRun: Constructor captures `t0`; loop runs; `main()` exits -> `~ScopeTimer()` captures `t1` and prints `t1 - t0`.
commonMistakes: Using `system_clock` (wall clock can jump!) instead of `steady_clock`.
followUp: *Should `ScopeTimer` be copyable?* (No—`ScopeTimer(const ScopeTimer&) = delete;` avoids duplicate prints!)

title: `Book` Class with `const` and Non-`const` Overloaded Methods
problemStatement: Create a `Book` class with `title` and `price`. Track how many times `getTitle()` was read—even on `const Book` objects!
constraints: Use modern C++17, avoid memory leaks, preserve const-correctness.
hint: Mark `views_` as `mutable`.
explanation: `b` is `const`, so only `const` methods can be called. `mutable views_` allows internal instrumentation without changing the logical state of `Book`.
dryRun: First `b.getTitle()` increments `views_` to `1`; second increments to `2`; `getViews()` returns `2`.
commonMistakes: Trying to increment non-`mutable` `views_` inside `const` method (compile error).
followUp: *If `b` is shared across threads, is `mutable int views_` safe?* (No—must be `mutable std::atomic<int> views_{0};`.)

title: Safe Dynamic Integer Wrapper (First Deep Copy Practice)
problemStatement: Write a `SafeInt` class holding an `int*` on the heap. Ensure copying `SafeInt b = a;` creates an independent copy with zero double-free.
constraints: Use modern C++17, avoid memory leaks, preserve const-correctness.
hint: Implement constructor, copy constructor, copy assignment, and destructor.
explanation: Each `SafeInt` owns its own `new int`. Mutating `b` leaves `a` intact, and both destruct cleanly.
dryRun: `a` allocates `10`; `b` allocates new `10`; `b.set(99)` writes only to `b.ptr_`; prints `a=10, b=99`.
commonMistakes: Forgetting `operator=` when writing copy constructor + destructor.
followUp: *How would Rule of 0 write this?* (Just use `int val_;` or `std::unique_ptr<int>` if heap is strictly needed.)

title: `Counter` Prefix and Postfix Increment Overloading
problemStatement: Implement a `Counter` class with `operator++()` (prefix) and `operator++(int)` (postfix) and `operator<<` for printing.
constraints: Use modern C++17, avoid memory leaks, preserve const-correctness.
hint: Postfix takes dummy `int` and returns previous copy by value.
explanation: Note separate `std::cout` statements keep evaluation order crystal clear. Prefix mutates and returns `*this` by ref; postfix saves `old` first.
dryRun: `c++` prints `5` (c becomes `6`); `c` prints `6`; `++c` increments to `7` and prints `7`.
commonMistakes: Returning `Counter&` from postfix `operator++(int)` (dangling reference to `old`).
followUp: *Why do iterators prefer `++it` over `it++`?* (Avoids copying the iterator object.)

title: `Vector2D` with `friend` Scalar Multiplication
problemStatement: Create `Vector2D(x, y)` supporting `v1 + v2`, `2.0 * v1`, `v1 * 2.0`, and `std::cout << v1`.
constraints: Use modern C++17, avoid memory leaks, preserve const-correctness.
hint: Make `operator*(double, const Vector2D&)` a non-member `friend`.
explanation: Symmetric `operator*` lets scalars appear on either left or right. Hidden `friend` definitions keep code clean and fast.
commonMistakes: Making `operator*` a member only, which breaks `2.0 * v`.
followUp: *What is Argument-Dependent Lookup (ADL) and how do hidden friends benefit from it?*

title: Single Inheritance — `Person` -> `Employee`
problemStatement: Derive `Employee` (adds `empId`, `salary`) from `Person` (`name`, `age`), initializing base fields via initializer list and printing full info.
constraints: Use modern C++17, avoid memory leaks, preserve const-correctness.
hint: Call `Person(std::move(name), age)` in `Employee`'s initializer list.
explanation: Keeping `Person`'s fields `private` (accessed via `name()`/`age()`) preserves `Person`'s encapsulation even against subclasses.
dryRun: `Person("Riya", 24)` runs first, then `Employee` members initialize, then `display()` prints.
commonMistakes: Making all base fields `protected` unnecessarily (reduces encapsulation).
followUp: *What happens if `Person` has no default constructor and `Employee` forgets `: Person(...)`?* (Compile error.)
expectedStdout: Name: Riya, Age: 24, ID: E12, Salary: 65000

title: Access Modes Under `private` Inheritance + `using` Exposure
problemStatement: Create `Timer` with `start()` and `internalReset()`. Create `Stopwatch` using `private` inheritance from `Timer` that exposes **only** `start()` publicly, hiding `internalReset()`.
constraints: Use modern C++17, avoid memory leaks, preserve const-correctness.
hint: Write `using Timer::start;` inside `Stopwatch`'s `public:` section.
explanation: Under `private` inheritance, all `public` base methods turn `private`, and `using Timer::start;` selectively re-exposes `start` without exposing `internalReset` or allowing upcasting to `Timer*`.
dryRun: `sw.start()` prints `Timer started\n`.
commonMistakes: Using `public` inheritance when you don't want an "is-a" relationship.
followUp: *How would you achieve the exact same thing using Composition?* (Make `Timer t_;` private and write `void start() { t_.start(); }`—usually cleaner!)

title: `Car` Has-A `Engine` (Composition)
problemStatement: Model a `Car` that owns an `Engine(horsepower)` by value, starting the engine via `Car::drive()`.
constraints: Use modern C++17, avoid memory leaks, preserve const-correctness.
hint: Declare `Engine engine_;` directly inside `Car`.
explanation: `Engine` has no independent existence outside `Car`. Its lifetime is tied automatically to `Car`.
dryRun: `Car(150)` constructs `engine_(150)`; `c.drive()` calls `engine_.ignite()` then prints ` -> Car driving`.
commonMistakes: Inheriting `class Car : public Engine` ("a Car is an Engine"—false!).
followUp: *When would you replace `Engine engine_;` with `std::unique_ptr<IEngine>`?* (When swapping `ElectricEngine`/`PetrolEngine` polymorphically.)

title: Simple `Calculator` Function Overloading
problemStatement: Build a `Calculator` class with overloaded `add` methods for: two `int`s, three `int`s, two `double`s, and a `const std::vector<int>&`.
constraints: Use modern C++17, avoid memory leaks, preserve const-correctness.
hint: Keep parameter types unambiguous (avoid `add(int, int, int = 0)` alongside `add(int, int)`!).
explanation: All 4 `add` methods share a clean interface while resolving at compile time with zero runtime overhead.
dryRun: Calls resolve cleanly to `(int,int)`, `(int,int,int)`, `(double,double)`, and `vector<int>` via brace-init `{1,2,3,4,5}`.
complexity: Time $O(1)$ for fixed args, $O(N)$ for vector; Space $O(1)$ extra.
commonMistakes: Adding default arguments that collide with 2-arg overload (`calc.add(2, 3)` becomes ambiguous).
followUp: *Could a template `template <typename T> T add(T a, T b)` replace the `(int,int)` and `(double,double)` overloads?*

title: `Logger` Singleton Pattern (Meyers' Thread-Safe Singleton)
problemStatement: Implement a thread-safe `Logger` singleton that allows only one instance in the entire application and counts logged messages.
constraints: Use modern C++17, avoid memory leaks, preserve const-correctness.
hint: Delete copy/move operations and return a `static Logger instance;` inside `static Logger& get()`.
explanation: Private constructor stops direct instantiation; deleting copy ctor also suppresses move ops. C++11 magic statics guarantee thread-safe one-time initialization.
dryRun: First `get()` creates `instance`; logs `[1] Booted`; second `get()` reuses same `instance`; logs `[2] Ready`.
commonMistakes: Returning `Logger` by value instead of `Logger&`, or forgetting `= delete` on copy constructor.
followUp: *Why do some senior engineers consider Singleton an anti-pattern in unit testing?* (Global mutable state makes tests coupled; prefer Dependency Injection where possible.)

title: `BankAccount` Hierarchy with Savings & Checking Polymorphism
problemStatement: Create a `BankAccount` base class (`deposit`, `virtual bool withdraw`, `virtual void monthEnd`, `virtual ~BankAccount`) and derive `SavingsAccount` (adds interest, forbids overdraft) and `CheckingAccount` (allows overdraft up to a limit).
constraints: Use modern C++17, avoid memory leaks, preserve const-correctness.
hint: Protect `balance_` via controlled `protected` helpers or `protected` balance with strict validation.
explanation: `std::vector<std::unique_ptr<BankAccount>>` holds heterogeneous accounts without slicing and destroys them safely via `virtual ~BankAccount()`.
dryRun: Savings `1000` -> `monthEnd()` adds `5%` -> `1050`. Checking `100` withdraws `300` (within `100+500=600`) -> `-200`.
complexity: Time $O(1)$ per account op, Space $O(N)$ accounts.
commonMistakes: Using `std::vector<BankAccount>` (causes object slicing!).
followUp: *Why should `BankAccount` forbid copy/assignment if used polymorphically?* (Prevents slicing when assigning `*accounts[0] = *accounts[1]`.)

title: `Complex` Number Class with Full Operator Overloading
problemStatement: Implement `Complex(real, imag)` supporting `+`, `-`, `*`, `==`, `!=`, `+=`, and `<<` (`3 + 4i` or `3 - 4i`).
constraints: Use modern C++17, avoid memory leaks, preserve const-correctness.
hint: Implement `+=` as member, `+` in terms of `+=` as non-member.
explanation: Non-member `friend` operators permit `2.0 + a` via implicit `Complex(double)` constructor. Floating-point epsilon avoids `==` precision surprises.
commonMistakes: Using exact `==` on floating-point numbers or making `operator<<` a member.
followUp: *Why take `lhs` by value in `operator+(Complex lhs, const Complex& rhs)`?* (Reuses the copy parameter directly for `lhs += rhs` and enables move elision on `a + b + c`.)

title: `Shape` Abstract Class Hierarchy (`Circle`, `Rectangle`, `Triangle`)
problemStatement: Create an abstract `Shape` with `area()`, `perimeter()`, and `name()`, implement 3 concrete shapes, and write a function `totalArea(const std::vector<std::unique_ptr<Shape>>&)` summing areas.
constraints: Use modern C++17, avoid memory leaks, preserve const-correctness.
hint: Every `Shape` method should be `const = 0;`, plus `virtual ~Shape() = default;`.
explanation: `Shape` defines a strict contract; `final` on leaf classes enables devirtualization when used directly.
commonMistakes: Missing `const` on overrides (`double area() override` fails to override `double area() const = 0`).
followUp: *Why didn't we use `M_PI`?* (`M_PI` is non-standard POSIX; `constexpr double PI` is portable C++17.)

title: `DynamicIntArray` with Deep Copy & Copy Assignment (Rule of 3)
problemStatement: Implement a `DynamicIntArray(size, initVal)` owning a raw `int*` buffer, supporting deep copy construction, exception-safe copy assignment, bounds-checked `at()`, and `operator[]`.
constraints: Use modern C++17, avoid memory leaks, preserve const-correctness.
hint: Allocate the new array *before* `delete[] data_;` in `operator=`.
explanation: Strong exception safety: if `new int[rhs.size_]` throws `std::bad_alloc`, `a`'s old `data_` and `size_` remain intact. Handles `size_ == 0` gracefully without dereferencing `nullptr`.
commonMistakes: Using `delete data_;` instead of `delete[] data_;`!
followUp: *How can Copy-and-Swap shorten `operator=` even further?*

title: Employee Payroll System Using `virtual` Inheritance & Overriding
problemStatement: Model `Employee` (`name`, `id`, `virtual double calculatePay() const = 0`) with `FullTimeEmployee` (monthly salary + bonus) and `ContractEmployee` (hours * hourlyRate).
constraints: Use modern C++17, avoid memory leaks, preserve const-correctness.
hint: Keep `calculatePay()` pure virtual so generic `Employee` cannot be instantiated directly.
explanation: Payroll loop doesn't care if an employee is full-time or contractor—open for extension (e.g., `CommissionEmployee`) without modifying the payroll loop.
commonMistakes: Putting `hours_` or `bonus_` in base `Employee` class.
followUp: *How would you support tax calculation that varies by country?* (Inject an `ITaxStrategy`—Composition!)

title: Friend Function Comparing Two Separate Classes (`Savings` & `Current`)
problemStatement: Write a `friend` function `totalFunds(const Savings&, const Current&)` that accesses private balances of two unrelated classes without exposing public balance getters.
constraints: Use modern C++17, avoid memory leaks, preserve const-correctness.
hint: Forward-declare `class Current;` before defining `class Savings`.
explanation: Forward declaration lets `Savings` name `const Current&` inside the `friend` signature before `Current` is fully defined.
commonMistakes: Forgetting `class Current;` forward declaration before `Savings`.
followUp: *Could a shared base `Account` remove the need for `friend` here?* (Yes—if both share a common abstraction!)

title: `Matrix` Class with `operator()` Access & Multiplication
problemStatement: Create a `Matrix(rows, cols)` using a single contiguous 1D `std::vector<double>` (Rule of 0!), overloading `(r, c)` for read/write and `*` for matrix multiplication.
constraints: Use modern C++17, avoid memory leaks, preserve const-correctness.
hint: Map `(r, c)` to `r * cols_ + c` for cache-friendly contiguous storage!
explanation: Using `std::vector<double>` gives full Rule of 0 (copy, move, destructor all free!). `i-k-j` loop order maximizes CPU cache locality. Also note `operator[]` only took 1 index in C++17 (2D `operator[]` wasn't added until C++23), so `operator()(r, c)` is the idiomatic C++17 choice!
complexity: Multiplication Time $O(R_A \cdot C_A \cdot C_B)$, Space $O(R_A \cdot C_B)$.
commonMistakes: Using `std::vector<std::vector<double>>` (poor cache locality, jagged allocations) or trying `operator[](r, c)` in C++17.
followUp: *Why is `i-k-j` loop order faster than `i-j-k`?* (Sequential row access in `B` and `C` instead of strided column jumps in `B`.)

title: Aggregation — `Department` and Independent `Professor`s
problemStatement: Model `Professor` and `Department`. When a `Department` is destroyed, `Professor` survives; if a `Professor` retires (is destroyed), `Department` safely skips them when listing faculty!
exampleOutput: `Active Faculty: Dr. Rao` (after Dr. Sen retires)
constraints: Use modern C++17, avoid memory leaks, preserve const-correctness.
hint: Store `std::vector<std::weak_ptr<Professor>>` inside `Department`.
explanation: `Department` does not own `Professor`s. `wp.lock()` safely checks liveness without keeping retired professors alive or crashing on dangling pointers.
dryRun: `p2.reset()` drops `Dr. Sen`'s refcount to 0 -> destroyed. `listActiveFaculty()` locks `p1` (valid), fails to lock `p2` (skips). `cs` dies; `p1` still prints `Dr. Rao`.
commonMistakes: Storing `Professor*` and dereferencing after `p2` is destroyed!
followUp: *How can `Department` lazily clean up expired `weak_ptr` entries?* (Erase-remove idiom using `wp.expired()`.)
expectedStdout:
CS Active Faculty: Dr. Rao 
Still alive: Dr. Rao

title: Bidirectional Association `Student` <-> `Course` Without Duplicates
problemStatement: Model `Student` and `Course` where enrolling a student updates both sides consistently (`student.courses()` and `course.students()`) with no duplicate enrollments.
constraints: Use modern C++17, avoid memory leaks, preserve const-correctness.
hint: Use a single coordinator method `enroll(Student&, Course&)` or `Course::enroll(Student&)` so one side cannot go out of sync.
explanation: `EnrollmentManager` as a `friend` acts as the single source of truth updating both vectors atomically, preventing half-linked states.
dryRun: First `enroll` adds `&c` to `s.courses_` and `&s` to `c.students_`. Second call sees `&c` present and returns `false`.
complexity: Time $O(N)$ duplicate check (or $O(1)$ with `unordered_set`), Space $O(E)$ enrollments.
commonMistakes: Letting callers modify `s.courses_` directly without updating `c.students_`.
followUp: *What happens if a `Student` object is destroyed while `Course` still holds `Student*`?* (Need unenroll in `~Student()`, or an `Enrollment` association table with IDs!)

title: `Library` Item Polymorphic Search & Checkout
problemStatement: Model `LibraryItem` (`id`, `title`, `borrowed`, `virtual int loanDays() const = 0`) with `Book` (14 days) and `Magazine` (7 days), plus a `Library` supporting `checkout(id)`.
constraints: Use modern C++17, avoid memory leaks, preserve const-correctness.
hint: Keep borrow/return logic once in `LibraryItem` rather than duplicating in `Book` and `Magazine`.
explanation: `using LibraryItem::LibraryItem;` cleanly inherits base constructors without boilerplate. `Library` owns items via `unique_ptr`.
dryRun: First `checkoutById(1)` succeeds -> prints 14 days; second finds `borrowed_ == true` -> prints `Item unavailable`.
commonMistakes: Copying `unique_ptr` by value into `add` without `std::move`.
followUp: *How would you compute overdue fines differently per item type?* (Add `virtual double finePerDay() const = 0;`.)
expectedStdout:
Checked out: Clean Code (14 days)
Item unavailable

title: Multiple Interfaces (`IPrintable` & `ISerializable`)
problemStatement: Define two interfaces `IPrintable` (`print() const`) and `ISerializable` (`toJson() const`), implement both in `Invoice`, and write separate functions accepting each interface.
constraints: Use modern C++17, avoid memory leaks, preserve const-correctness.
hint: Every interface gets `virtual ~Interface() = default;`.
explanation: Clients `render` and `save` only depend on the minimal interface they actually need (ISP + DIP), with zero diamond state.
dryRun: `render(inv)` calls `Invoice::print()`; `save(inv)` calls `Invoice::toJson()`.
commonMistakes: Merging `print` and `toJson` into one fat `IDocument` interface.
followUp: *Does `Invoice` have two `vptr`s in memory here?* (Yes—typically one for `IPrintable` subobject and one for `ISerializable` subobject!)

title: Function Hiding Fixed via `using Base::log;`
problemStatement: Create `BaseLogger` with `log(int code)` and `log(const std::string& msg)`. Derive `TaggedLogger` adding `log(const std::string& tag, const std::string& msg)` while keeping both base overloads callable!
constraints: Use modern C++17, avoid memory leaks, preserve const-correctness.
hint: Add `using BaseLogger::log;` inside `TaggedLogger`.
explanation: Without `using BaseLogger::log;`, `logger.log(404)` and `logger.log("Boot")` would fail to compile because `TaggedLogger::log(tag, msg)` takes 2 args and hides all 1-arg `BaseLogger::log` overloads!
dryRun: All 3 calls resolve cleanly across the combined overload set.
commonMistakes: Assuming inheritance automatically merges overload sets across scopes.
followUp: *What if `BaseLogger::log(int)` were `private`?* (`using BaseLogger::log;` would fail to compile because you cannot expose private base members!)

title: Custom `String` Class — Deep Copy, `operator=`, `operator+`, `operator<<`
problemStatement: Implement a minimal `MyString` managing `char* data_` manually (C-style null-terminated string) with constructor, copy constructor, copy assignment, destructor, `operator+`, and `operator<<`.
constraints: Use modern C++17, avoid memory leaks, preserve const-correctness.
hint: Always allocate `len + 1` bytes for the `'\0'` terminator!
explanation: Uses copy-and-swap for `operator=`, handles `nullptr` safely, and copies exact `len_ + 1` bytes including `'\0'`.
dryRun: `a+b` allocates 12 bytes `"Hello World\0"`; `a = c` copies `c` into `rhs`, swaps buffers, and old `"Hello"` is deleted when `rhs` dies.
commonMistakes: Allocating `new char[len_]` instead of `len_ + 1` (off-by-one heap buffer overflow!).
followUp: *Add a `noexcept` move constructor `MyString(MyString&&)`—what must `o.data_` be set to?* (Don't leave `o.data_ == nullptr` if `operator<<` assumes `data_` is non-null, OR guard `data_ ? data_ : ""`—setting `new char[1]{'\0'}` or guarding `nullptr` avoids UB!)

title: `DiscountStrategy` Using Composition (Strategy Pattern)
problemStatement: Implement a `ShoppingCart` whose discount policy (`NoDiscount`, `FlatDiscount`, `PercentDiscount`) can be swapped at runtime without subclassing `ShoppingCart`.
constraints: Use modern C++17, avoid memory leaks, preserve const-correctness.
hint: Hold `std::unique_ptr<IDiscountStrategy>` inside `ShoppingCart`.
explanation: Instead of creating `PercentShoppingCart` and `FlatShoppingCart` subclasses, composition lets `cart` switch algorithms dynamically!
dryRun: `1000` with 20% off -> `800`; swapped to flat 100 off -> `900`.
commonMistakes: Hardcoding `if (type == PERCENT) ...` inside `ShoppingCart`.
followUp: *When could `std::function<double(double)>` replace `IDiscountStrategy`?* (For stateless/single-method strategies, lambdas are even lighter!)

title: `inline static` Registry Tracking Active Instances
problemStatement: Create a `Device` class whose constructor registers `this` into an `inline static std::vector<Device*>` and destructor removes `this` cleanly, with `Device::broadcast(msg)`.
exampleOutput: `[D1] Ping` and `[D2] Ping`, then after `D1` dies: `[D2] Ping2`
constraints: Use modern C++17, avoid memory leaks, preserve const-correctness.
hint: Delete copy/move or update the registry properly in copy/move constructors!
explanation: `inline static` avoids needing an out-of-class vector definition. Deleting copy/move prevents dangling `this` pointers if a `Device` moved in memory inside a container.
dryRun: `d2` registers, `d1` registers -> `broadcast("Ping")` prints both; `d1` leaves scope and removes `&d1`; `broadcast("Ping2")` prints only `d2`.
commonMistakes: Leaving copy constructor enabled, or forgetting to remove `this` in `~Device()` (dangling pointer crash!).
followUp: *What happens if `Device` is stored in `std::vector<Device>` and the vector reallocates?* (Addresses move, invalidating `this`! Either forbid moving/copying and use `unique_ptr<Device>`, or update `registry_` in move ctor!)

title: `Fraction` Class with `operator<=>` Style Comparisons (`==`, `<`, `<<`)
problemStatement: Build a `Fraction(num, den)` that reduces automatically via `std::gcd`, rejects `den == 0`, keeps `den > 0`, and overloads `+`, `==`, `<`, and `<<`.
constraints: Use modern C++17, avoid memory leaks, preserve const-correctness.
hint: Normalize sign so `den_` is always positive before calling `std::gcd`.
explanation: `std::gcd` is built into C++17 `<numeric>`. Casting to `long long` in `operator<` prevents `int` overflow on cross-multiplication!
commonMistakes: Integer overflow in `a.num_ * b.den_` or forgetting negative denominators (`1/-2`).
followUp: *Why can `operator==` simply compare `num_` and `den_` directly instead of cross-multiplying?* (Because `reduce()` guarantees canonical form!)

title: Non-Virtual Interface (NVI) Template Method Pipeline
problemStatement: Design a `DataExporter` base class with a public non-virtual `exportReport()` that runs `open()`, `writeHeader()`, `writeBody()`, and `close()` in fixed order, where subclasses customize only `writeHeader()` and `writeBody()`.
constraints: Use modern C++17, avoid memory leaks, preserve const-correctness.
hint: Make `open()` and `close()` fixed in base, and `writeHeader()`/`writeBody()` `private virtual = 0`.
explanation: Subclasses *can* override `private virtual` methods even though they cannot call `DataExporter::writeHeader()`. The base class preserves total control over pre/post steps (`[OPEN]`/`[CLOSE]`).
dryRun: `exp.exportReport()` prints `[OPEN] `, dispatches virtually to `CsvExporter::writeHeader()` and `writeBody()`, then prints `[CLOSE]\n`.
commonMistakes: Thinking `private virtual` methods cannot be overridden in C++!
followUp: *What if a subclass wants optional custom behavior on `close()`?* (Make `onClose()` a `protected virtual` with an empty default body!)

title: Complete Rule of 5 `Buffer<int>` with `noexcept` Move Semantics
problemStatement: Implement a `Buffer` class managing a raw `int*` array with all 5 special member functions properly implemented and `noexcept` moves, plus verify `std::vector<Buffer>` moves instead of copies on reallocation.
constraints: Use modern C++17, avoid memory leaks, preserve const-correctness.
hint: Guard `if (this == &rhs) return *this;` in move assignment (`a = std::move(a);`) and leave moved-from `other.data_ = nullptr; other.size_ = 0;`.
explanation: Marking `Buffer(Buffer&&) noexcept` makes `std::vector` use `MoveCtor` instead of `CopyCtor` during capacity growth.
dryRun: First `push_back` moves temporary `Buffer(10)`. Second `push_back` triggers reallocation from cap 1 -> 2, moving `Buffer(10)` then moving `Buffer(20)`.
commonMistakes: Omitting `noexcept` on `Buffer(Buffer&&)`, causing `std::vector` to silently fall back to $O(N)$ `CopyCtor`!
followUp: *What happens if someone runs `b = std::move(b);` without `if (this == &rhs)`?* (`delete[] data_` frees its own buffer -> UB!)

title: Rule of 0 Refactoring Using `std::unique_ptr<int[]>`
concepts: move-only semantics vs deep copy wrapper.
problemStatement: Rewrite a resource-owning `AudioClip` class following **Rule of 0** (zero custom destructor/copy/move functions!) while owning a dynamic heap array of samples.
constraints: Use modern C++17, avoid memory leaks, preserve const-correctness.
hint: `std::vector<int>` gives copyable + movable Rule of 0; `std::unique_ptr<int[]>` gives move-only Rule of 0! Let's show `std::vector<int>` for full copy+move Rule of 0.
explanation: `std::string` and `std::vector<int>` already implement Rule of 5 safely. By composing them, `AudioClip` achieves Rule of 0: 0 memory leaks, automatic deep copy, automatic `noexcept` move, and clean code.
dryRun: `b` deep-copies 4 samples; `c` steals `a`'s internal buffer in $O(1)$.
commonMistakes: Adding `~AudioClip() = default;` and accidentally disabling move semantics!
followUp: *When can you NOT use Rule of 0?* (When writing a low-level RAII handle itself—like wrapping a C `FILE*` or OS socket—or writing `std::unique_ptr` itself!)

title: Diamond Inheritance Solved (`Device` -> `Scanner`, `Printer` -> `Copier`)
problemStatement: Model `PoweredDevice(serialNo)` inherited virtually by `Scanner` and `Printer`, and multiply inherited by `Copier`. Ensure only ONE `serialNo` exists and `Copier` initializes it cleanly.
constraints: Use modern C++17, avoid memory leaks, preserve const-correctness.
hint: Use `virtual public PoweredDevice` on `Scanner` and `Printer`, and call `PoweredDevice(serial)` directly in `Copier`'s initializer list.
explanation: `Scanner(0)` and `Printer(0)`'s `PoweredDevice(0)` calls are ignored when constructing `Copier`; `Copier`'s `PoweredDevice(777)` constructs the single shared base!
dryRun: `PoweredDevice(777)` runs once -> `Scanner` -> `Printer` -> `Copier`. `c.serial()` unambiguously returns `777`.
commonMistakes: Putting `virtual` on `Copier : virtual Scanner, virtual Printer` instead of on `Scanner` and `Printer`.
followUp: *Why can `dynamic_cast<Copier*>(poweredPtr)` succeed while `static_cast<Copier*>(poweredPtr)` fails to compile?*

title: Polymorphic `PaymentGateway` System Following SOLID
problemStatement: Build a payment checkout processor accepting any `IPaymentMethod` (`CreditCard`, `UPI`, `Wallet`), validating amounts, returning a `Receipt`, and allowing new payment methods with zero changes to `CheckoutService`.
constraints: Use modern C++17, avoid memory leaks, preserve const-correctness.
hint: Inject `IPaymentMethod&` (or `unique_ptr`) into `CheckoutService::process()`.
explanation: `CheckoutService` depends solely on `IPaymentMethod` (DIP) and never needs modification when `CryptoPayment` is added (OCP).
dryRun: `service.process(upi, 1500)` validates `> 0`, dispatches virtually to `UpiPayment::pay(1500)`, prints `[UPI: user@ok] Paid 1500`.
commonMistakes: Switching on `enum PaymentType { CARD, UPI }` inside `CheckoutService`.
followUp: *How would you add refund support without forcing a `GiftCard` (non-refundable) to implement `refund()`?* (ISP: create a separate `IRefundable` interface!)

title: Virtual Constructor (`clone()` Idiom) for Polymorphic Deep Copy
problemStatement: Given `std::vector<std::unique_ptr<Document>>`, implement a `Document` hierarchy (`PdfDoc`, `WordDoc`) supporting deep-copying an entire polymorphic `DocumentList` without knowing concrete types!
constraints: Use modern C++17, avoid memory leaks, preserve const-correctness.
hint: Declare `virtual std::unique_ptr<Document> clone() const = 0;` on `Document`.
explanation: Because constructors cannot be `virtual`, `clone()` uses runtime dispatch to call the concrete copy constructor (`PdfDoc(*this)`).
dryRun: `Folder f2 = f1` loops over `f1.docs_`, calling `clone()` -> constructs an independent `PdfDoc("v1")` for `f2`.
commonMistakes: Copying `std::unique_ptr` directly (compile error) or trying `std::make_unique<Document>(*d)` (slices or fails on abstract class!).
followUp: *Why can't `clone()` use covariant return type `std::unique_ptr<PdfDoc>` when overriding `std::unique_ptr<Document>`?*

title: Custom RAII `UniqueFile` Handle (Non-Copyable, Movable)
problemStatement: Wrap C's `std::FILE*` in a safe `UniqueFile` class that closes automatically on destruction, forbids copying (`= delete`), and allows moving (`noexcept`).
constraints: Use modern C++17, avoid memory leaks, preserve const-correctness.
hint: On move assignment, close any currently open `file_` before taking over `rhs.file_`, and set `rhs.file_ = nullptr;`.
explanation: `std::exchange(other.fp_, nullptr)` atomically steals the handle and nulls out the source in one clean C++14/17 call. Destructor checks `if (fp_)` before `fclose`.
dryRun: Moving transfers ownership without duplicating `FILE*` (which would cause double-`fclose` UB!).
commonMistakes: Calling `std::fclose(nullptr)` (UB in C!) or allowing copying of raw `FILE*`.
followUp: *Why could you also write this in 2 lines using Rule of 0 with `std::unique_ptr<std::FILE, decltype(&std::fclose)>`?*
expectedStdout: UniqueFile RAII compiled with move-only semantics

title: Custom `SmartPtr<T>` (`UniquePtr` Simplified)
problemStatement: Implement a simplified `UniquePtr<T>` managing a single `T*` with `get()`, `release()`, `reset()`, `*`, `->`, move constructor/assignment, and deleted copy operations.
constraints: Use modern C++17, avoid memory leaks, preserve const-correctness.
hint: Mark `operator bool()` as `explicit` so `UniquePtr<int> p; int x = p;` doesn't compile accidentally!
explanation: Look at `reset`: exchanging `ptr_` *before* `delete old` guarantees `ptr_` is already updated even if `~T()` indirectly inspects this `UniquePtr`!
dryRun: `p1` owns `Box(42)`; `std::move(p1)` transfers pointer to `p2` and nulls `p1`; `p2->x` prints `42`.
commonMistakes: Not checking `this != &rhs` in `operator=(UniquePtr&&)` or `delete ptr_` before updating `ptr_` in `reset`.
followUp: *Why does `std::unique_ptr` support custom deleters as a template parameter while `std::shared_ptr` type-erases the deleter?*

title: Intrusive / Manual Reference-Counted `SharedBox`
problemStatement: Build a simplified `SharedInt` holding `int* val_` and `int* refCount_` to demonstrate how `std::shared_ptr` manages shared ownership, deep-decrementing on copy/assign/destruction.
constraints: Use modern C++17, avoid memory leaks, preserve const-correctness.
hint: Write a private `release()` helper called by both `~SharedInt()` and `operator=`.
explanation: Centralizing decrement-and-delete inside `release()` eliminates duplicate cleanup logic across copy assign, move assign, and destructor.
dryRun: `a` starts `count=1`; `b=a` increments `count=2`; `b` leaves scope -> `count=1` (doesn't delete `50`); `main` exits -> `count=0` deletes both `val_` and `count_`.
complexity: Time $O(1)$, Space $O(1)$ per handle + 1 control int.
commonMistakes: Forgetting `if (this == &rhs)` (calling `release()` when `count == 1` would delete `val_` before re-assigning!) or using non-atomic `int` in multi-threaded code.
followUp: *Why is `std::make_shared<int>(50)` faster than `SharedInt(50)`?* (Single combined heap allocation for object + control block!)

title: Safe Copy Assignment with Strong Exception Guarantee & Self-Assignment
problemStatement: Implement a `Packet` class holding `id` + dynamically allocated payload (`std::size_t len`, `unsigned char* bytes`) where `operator=` guarantees `*this` is completely unchanged if allocation throws, and handles `p = p;` safely.
constraints: Use modern C++17, avoid memory leaks, preserve const-correctness.
hint: Copy-allocate the new buffer *completely* before mutating `this->bytes_` or `this->len_`.
explanation: Commit-or-rollback pattern: all throwing operations (`new[]`) execute first; non-throwing pointer swaps/deletes execute afterward.
dryRun: `p2 = p1` allocates 3 bytes, copies `0xAA`, deletes old 5-byte buffer; `p2 = p2` returns immediately.
commonMistakes: Calling `delete[] bytes_` *before* `new unsigned char[rhs.len_]`!
followUp: *When does this manual pattern beat Copy-and-Swap?* (When you can reuse `this->bytes_` if `rhs.len_ <= capacity_` without allocating!)

title: Scott Meyers `const_cast` + `std::as_const` Pattern in `SafeGrid`
problemStatement: Implement a `SafeGrid` where both `const` and non-`const` `at(r, c)` share a single bounds-checking implementation cleanly without code duplication or Undefined Behavior.
constraints: Use modern C++17, avoid memory leaks, preserve const-correctness.
hint: Implement the `const` `at()` fully, and have non-`const` `at()` call `const_cast<int&>(std::as_const(*this).at(r, c))`.
explanation: Non-`const` `at()` knows `*this` is genuinely non-`const`, so casting away `const` on the returned reference is 100% UB-free.
dryRun: `g.at(1,1)` calls `const` `at(1,1)`, checks bounds, casts to `int&`, writes `42`; `cg.at(1,1)` calls `const` `at(1,1)` directly and prints `42`.
commonMistakes: Doing the reverse (calling non-`const` from `const`)—which could cause UB on a true `const` object!
followUp: *Why didn't we forget `std::as_const(*this)` and write `this->at(r, c)`?* (Calling `this->at(r, c)` inside non-const `at()` would call itself infinitely -> stack overflow!)

title: Polymorphic Plugin Factory Using `inline static` Registration Map
problemStatement: Design a `CompressorFactory` using `inline static` registry + `std::unique_ptr<ICompressor>` so new formats (`Zip`, `Gzip`) can register without editing `create()`.
constraints: Use modern C++17, avoid memory leaks, preserve const-correctness.
hint: Store `std::function<std::unique_ptr<ICompressor>()>` creators in an `inline static std::unordered_map`.
explanation: Eliminates the classic `if (key == "zip") ... else if (key == "gzip") ...` OCP violation completely!
dryRun: Registers lambdas for `"zip"` and `"gzip"`, then dynamically instantiates each via `create(fmt)`.
complexity: Time $O(1)$ average lookup, Space $O(K)$ registered types.
commonMistakes: Returning raw `ICompressor*` (unclear ownership) instead of `std::unique_ptr<ICompressor>`.
followUp: *What happens if two `.cpp` files register into `registry_` before `main()`?* (SIOF! Solve by wrapping `registry_` inside a function-local `static` map instead of `inline static`!)

title: Observer Pattern (Event Bus) Using `std::weak_ptr`
problemStatement: Implement a `StockTicker` (Subject) notifying multiple `IObserver`s (`MobileApp`, `AlertBot`) when price changes, automatically pruning destroyed observers without crashing.
constraints: Use modern C++17, avoid memory leaks, preserve const-correctness.
hint: Store `std::vector<std::weak_ptr<IObserver>>` and lock each before notifying.
explanation: `weak_ptr` prevents memory leaks (ticker doesn't force observers to stay alive) and prevents dangling pointer crashes when `tempApp` goes out of scope.
dryRun: `tempApp` dies; `setPrice` locks `app` (prints once), fails to lock `tempApp` and erases its `weak_ptr`.
commonMistakes: Holding `IObserver*` without manual `unsubscribe()` in observer destructors (dangling pointer UB).
followUp: *What happens if an observer calls `subscribe()` inside `onPriceUpdate()`?* (Vector iterator invalidation! Copy snapshot or defer registrations.)

title: Passkey Idiom — Granular Access Control Better Than `friend class`
problemStatement: Allow `AuditService` to call ONLY `BankVault::auditInspect()` without giving `AuditService` direct access to `BankVault`'s private `cash_` or `setCash()`.
constraints: Use modern C++17, avoid memory leaks, preserve const-correctness.
hint: Create a nested `class AuditKey { AuditKey() = default; friend class AuditService; };` and require `AuditKey` as a parameter to `auditInspect`.
explanation: `AuditService` cannot touch `BankVault::cash_` directly, and `main()` cannot forge an `AuditKey{}`! Zero runtime overhead (empty `AuditKey` is optimized away).
dryRun: `AuditService` constructs `AuditKey{}` (allowed by `friend`), calls `auditInspect`, reads `50000`.
commonMistakes: Making `AuditKey()` `public` (defeats the gate!).
followUp: *Why make `AuditKey()` `= default;` instead of implicitly generated?* (An implicitly generated constructor is `public`, whereas `private: AuditKey() = default;` keeps it locked!)

title: Decorator Pattern Using Composition + Polymorphism
problemStatement: Build a `Coffee` ordering system where `Espresso` (`100`) can be dynamically wrapped with `MilkDecorator` (`+20`) and `CaramelDecorator` (`+30`) without subclass explosion (`EspressoWithMilkAndCaramel`).
constraints: Use modern C++17, avoid memory leaks, preserve const-correctness.
hint: `CoffeeDecorator` BOTH *is-a* `ICoffee` AND *has-a* `std::unique_ptr<ICoffee>`.
explanation: Avoids $2^N$ subclasses by chaining wrappers via `unique_ptr<ICoffee>`. Destruction unwinds cleanly from outer decorator to `Espresso`.
dryRun: `Caramel` delegates to `Milk` delegates to `Espresso`: `100 + 20 + 30 = 150`.
commonMistakes: Creating `EspressoMilk`, `EspressoCaramel`, `EspressoMilkCaramel` via inheritance.
followUp: *How is Decorator different from Inheritance?* (Composition adds responsibilities dynamically per object at runtime; inheritance adds statically to the entire class.)

title: PIMPL Idiom Implementation (Header-Safe Compilation Firewall)
problemStatement: Write a `DatabaseClient` class demonstrating the PIMPL pattern cleanly (struct `Impl` forward-declared in the public class, defined separately, with out-of-line destructor/move).
constraints: Use modern C++17, avoid memory leaks, preserve const-correctness.
hint: Declare `~DatabaseClient();` and move ops inside the class, and define them **after** `struct DatabaseClient::Impl` is complete!
explanation: If `~DatabaseClient()` were defaulted inline inside the header, `std::unique_ptr<Impl>`'s deleter would call `sizeof(Impl)` on an incomplete type and fail to compile! Defining `= default` after `struct Impl` fixes it.
dryRun: `DatabaseClient("prod_db")` allocates `Impl` on heap; `connect()` reads `pImpl_->connStr`; `~DatabaseClient()` destroys `Impl`.
commonMistakes: Omitting `~DatabaseClient();` in the class declaration when using `std::unique_ptr<Impl>`.
followUp: *What happens if you want `DatabaseClient` to also be copyable?* (Define custom copy ctor/assign after `Impl` that allocates `std::make_unique<Impl>(*other.pImpl_)`!)

title: Thread-Safe `BankAccount` with `mutable std::mutex` (`const` Correctness)
problemStatement: Make `ThreadSafeAccount` safe for concurrent `deposit`, `withdraw`, and `balance() const` reads—showing why `std::mutex` must be `mutable`!
constraints: Use modern C++17, avoid memory leaks, preserve const-correctness.
hint: `balance() const` must lock the mutex to read safely, which mutates the mutex!
explanation: Without `mutable`, `readView.balance() const` couldn't lock `mtx_` because locking changes `mtx_`'s internal state. `std::lock_guard` is RAII, guaranteeing unlock even on early `return` or exception.
commonMistakes: Returning `const double&` from `balance() const` (once `lock_guard` unlocks at `}`, caller would hold a reference without lock protection—return `double` by value!).
followUp: *What happens if `withdraw()` called `balance()` while already holding `mtx_`?* (**Deadlock!** Because `std::mutex` is non-recursive—never call another locking public method while holding the lock.)

title: Polymorphic `LRUCache` / `ICache` Following Rule of 0 + DIP + `inline static` Stats
problemStatement: Implement an `ICache<int, std::string>` interface and a concrete `LRUCache` (capacity $C$, $O(1)$ `get`/`put`) that tracks total cache hits via an `inline static` counter.
constraints: Use modern C++17, avoid memory leaks, preserve const-correctness.
hint: Store `(key, value)` pairs in `std::list` and iterators in `std::unordered_map`, splicing accessed nodes to front in $O(1)$.
explanation: Combines OOP (`IStringCache` abstraction, `final`, C++17 `std::optional` & `inline static`) with DSA ($O(1)$ `splice` + hash map) while staying 100% Rule-of-0 leak-free. (Note: if `LRUCache` were copied, `map_` iterators would point to the old list—so either delete copy or note `std::list` iterator stability; in fact, wait—because `std::unordered_map<int, Iter>` stores iterators into `this->order_`, copying `LRUCache` via default copy would copy old iterators! Good catch: in a production `LRUCache`, either mark copy `= delete` or write a proper copy constructor!)
dryRun: `put(1), put(2)` -> `[2, 1]`. `get(1)` -> `[1, 2]`, `totalHits=1`. `put(3)` evicts `2` -> `[3, 1]`. `get(2)` returns `nullopt`.
commonMistakes: Copying `LRUCache` when `map_` holds iterators into `order_`! (Let's add `LRUCache(const LRUCache&) = delete; LRUCache& operator=(const LRUCache&) = delete;` or mention it—actually let's check: adding `= delete` makes it 100% bug-free!)
followUp: *Why would the default compiler-generated copy constructor break `LRUCache` above?* (Because `map_` holds `list::iterator`s pointing to the *source* object's `order_` list, not the copy's `order_` list—classic Rule of 3/5 edge case even with STL containers!)
